methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort (N=262, 193 <70 years, 69 ≥70 years) with prospectively maintained database. Poisson regression, cumulative logistic regression, and Cox proportional hazards models appropriately applied with adjustment for confounding variables. Log-rank tests for survival comparison. Includes landmark analyses to address immortal-time bias concepts. However, retrospective design, single-center origin, elective surgery only, and potential selection bias limit methodological rigor.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Directly addresses important clinical question of age-related outcomes in colorectal cancer surgery. Findings inform individualized treatment decision-making in elderly patients. Demonstrates age alone not independent predictor when adjusted for other factors. LoE limited by retrospective, single-center, elective-only design. Clear relevance to clinical practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Clear reporting of inclusion/exclusion criteria, statistical methods (Poisson, cumulative logistic, Cox regression), and results with confidence intervals and p-values. Effective use of tables and Kaplan-Meier curves. However, no explicit STROBE adherence statement. Data and code availability not mentioned. Limitations section comprehensive.

novelty_literature.justification: Age-related outcome analysis in colorectal cancer well-established in literature. Study confirms known findings (age not independent predictor when adjusted) with single-center Brazilian cohort. Limited novel contribution beyond regional perspective. Incremental rather than groundbreaking contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear presentation of epidemiological context, methods, results, and discussion. Thoughtful discussion of selection bias (healthy survivor bias) in surgical cohorts. Appropriate contextualization of findings. Good acknowledgment of study limitations including retrospective design, single-center origin, and generalizability concerns. Publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Large single-center cohort (N=262) with prospectively maintained database enabling comprehensive multivariable analysis
Addresses important clinical question about chronological age as treatment decision criterion in elderly colorectal cancer patients
Appropriate statistical methods (Poisson, logistic, Cox regression) with adjustment for confounding variables
Acknowledges and discusses inherent selection bias (healthy survivor bias) characteristic of surgical cohorts
Transparent about limitations and study design; findings contextualized appropriately within evidence base
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design from Brazil with limited generalizability to other healthcare systems and regions
Selection bias inherent in surgical cohort limits ability to infer outcomes for all elderly patients with colorectal cancer
Elective surgery only; findings not applicable to emergency presentations common in some elderly patients
Data on specific postoperative complications beyond ICU, reoperation, mortality not available
Lacks formal geriatric assessment (frailty scores, functional status, cognitive function); ASA and comorbidities limited proxies
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective analysis addressing important age-related outcome question with appropriate statistical methods. Limited novelty and single-center Brazilian origin. Suitable for Tier 3 journals (BMC Cancer, Current Oncology) as confirmatory regional study supporting age-individualized treatment approaches.
